claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was a Christian theologian and biblical scholar who lived from approximately 185 to 254 CE.
Origen was born in Alexandria, Egypt, and died in Tyre, Phoenicia.
Origen succeeded Clement as head of the Catechetical School in Alexandria.
The Fragmentum ex commentariis in Osee is a Greek fragment from Origen's commentary on the biblical book of Hosea.
The fragment survives in the Patrologia Graeca edition of J.-P. Migne.

Origen's commentaries, like other works of his, survive largely in fragments, often preserved in catenae (chains), which are Byzantine biblical commentaries formed by stringing together brief passages excerpted from older commentaries.
Origen's approach to biblical commentary involved establishing the literal sense of the text through grammatical techniques, which then provided the basis for an elevated or spiritual sense.
Origen was the most important theologian and biblical scholar of the early Greek church, and his greatest work is the Hexapla, a synopsis of six versions of the Old Testament.
Origen made copious use of the allegorical method in his commentaries and laid the foundations of philosophical theology for the church.
The fragment from the Commentary on Hosea addresses grammatical and interpretive difficulties in the biblical text, including discussion of what appears to be solecisms in Scripture.
